title: [D1 Ingest] Capture replay driver through the live ingestion path
summary: A retained capture can now be put back through the pipeline: `scripts/replay_capture.py --captures <dir> <sha256> [--rate N] [--ingest]` publishes the capture's records to the ingest topic in the sensor's own wire form, optionally runs the ingestion side in the same process, and prints the four reconciled counters. The two halves of the wire — `publish_capture` and `consume_ingest_topic` — live in `helena.normalizer` beside the code live traffic already uses, so there is one adapter, one `_stamp` and one pair of stores rather than a replay pipeline beside the real one.
assumption_validated: Three, all measured. (1) 'Replay exercises the real pipeline rather than a parallel one' is checkable as rows, not as intent: the events a broker replay leaves in the store are compared against the events the same capture produces read straight off disk, and they are equal. (2) A capture replayed twice produces identical rows — over the wire, through both stores, including the quarantine row for a record the adapter refuses. Verified in the suite and by hand: the ten-record fixture replayed twice through the command left ten events with an identical (offset, event_id) digest. (3) NEGATIVE, and it corrects a concept note: `concept/06-technology.md` says a view added later 'starts empty rather than backfilling; adding one to a running deployment requires replay from the retained captures'. Measured against the pinned engine on 2026-09-04 — with ten events in `helena_normalized_events`, a materialized view created over that table reported all ten the moment it was created and picked up a later replay's record incrementally. The note is right about a view over a stream and wrong for this architecture, because since migration 0004 the normalized events are a TABLE in the single store. The rule that survives is narrower and is what the runbook now documents: what never reached the store cannot be recovered from the broker, only from the capture.
makes_buildable: Task 12 (flatten-layer views) can populate a throwaway store from a capture in one call and, more usefully, does not have to be written before the data exists — a flatten view added over `helena_normalized_events` backfills, measured. Any later view layer (signal, analytical) inherits that. `publish_capture` is also the only producer this project has for the ingest topic, so anything that needs records on the topic — a live-consumer daemon, a load or latency measurement, an evaluation run — uses it rather than open-coding the headers. `consume_ingest_topic` is the consumer half a daemon would call, already the only place a wire message becomes an ingest message.

verification.detail: 445 passed (434 before, so 11 new), run twice: once with scripts/dev-up already running, once cold with nothing up so the conftest fixtures start their own engine and broker. `uv lock --check` and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` also clean. Nine of the new tests are marked `integration` and go over the pinned blink and into a real RisingWave. Run by hand as well, against the persistent engine and broker with the real .env: `uv run scripts/replay_capture.py --captures tests/fixtures/captures <hash> --rate 5 --ingest` reported records=10 consumed=10 normalized=10 quarantined=0 and 'every record of the capture reached the store' in 8.0 s (10 records at 5/s is 1.8 s of pacing plus the 5 s idle timeout); a second run of the same command left the same ten rows with an identical (record_offset, event_id) digest; a second capture replayed afterwards was picked up incrementally by a materialized view created between the two runs. The store was empty before and was left empty. Mutation-checked, three mutations, all caught: dropping the pacer (the rate test fails, and the unpaced control is what makes it mean something), dropping the last record of the capture (six tests fail, including the command's), and making the event id non-deterministic (the replayed-twice test fails on the row comparison). One mutation deliberately not attempted: removing the `flush()` inside `publish_capture` is invisible to the suite because every caller is inside a `with BrokerProducer(...)` block that flushes on exit — the flush is there so the returned count is honest for a caller that is not.

escalations.detail: The PRD asks for `helena replay-capture <hash>`. There is no `helena` console entry point in this project and one was not added: a command dispatcher with exactly one subcommand is the 'registry for a second case that does not exist' `concept/instruction.md` §1 forbids, and `scripts/migrate.py` is the project's existing 'run it by hand' surface. The capability is identical and the argparse `prog` is `replay-capture`; the invocation is `uv run scripts/replay_capture.py`. If a second command is ever written, promoting both to a `helena` entry point is the increment that earns it.

The capture directory is a required `--captures DIR` argument rather than a new `HELENA_CAPTURE_DIRECTORY` variable. A required variable would fail startup for every deployment including the ones that never replay, and `Settings.load` resolves all or nothing; a CLI argument with no default keeps the fail-loud property where it belongs. This is recorded rather than assumed because 'where the retained captures live' is deployment knowledge, and the moment a second thing needs it — a live producer, an evaluation harness — it becomes configuration.

With `--ingest`, the replay process is also the consumer. That is correct today because nothing else consumes the ingest topic, but it means replay into a deployment that HAS a live consumer must be run without `--ingest` and the counters then come from whatever is consuming. The reconciliation is per capture and refuses a set that does not add up, so a topic carrying another producer's records during a verified run is reported as a failure to reconcile rather than folded into the numbers. Where a long-running consumer lives is still task 10's deferred item, not answered here.
The concept/05 vs data/netify tension noted in CONTEXT.md §3 was not touched by this task and remains as ADR-0009 left it.

invariant_conflicts.step: Document replay as the procedure for backfilling a newly added view
invariant_conflicts.conflict: The procedure as the concept notes state it does not hold in this architecture, and the documentation says so rather than repeating it. `concept/06-technology.md` (and docs/runbook.md §5, which followed it) said a view added after ingest starts 'begins empty and stays that way ... there is no backlog to re-read it from'. Measured 2026-09-04: a materialized view created over `helena_normalized_events` backfills from the table and is maintained incrementally afterwards. The note's claim is true of a view over a stream; normalized events have been a table in the single store since migration 0004. `concept/` outranks the code, so this is reported as a discrepancy for the operator to settle in the note rather than fixed in `concept/`: docs/runbook.md §5 and §8 now carry the measurement and the narrower rule (what never reached the store cannot be recovered from the broker, only from the capture), and README says the same.
See the first escalation. The command exists and does what the step asks; it is spelled `uv run scripts/replay_capture.py` because a one-subcommand dispatcher is the abstraction §1 forbids.

deferred: A `helena` console entry point, and a Makefile target. `make migrate` takes no arguments; a replay target would need CAPTURES and a hash, which is a configuration surface for one command.

A long-running consumer. `--ingest` drains the topic once and stops on the idle timeout, which is what a bounded, reconcilable run is; a daemon is still task 10's deferred item and still has no caller.

Replaying a directory, a range of captures, or a time window. One capture per invocation; a loop in a shell covers the rest, and 'which captures cover this window' needs a capture index, which would be the second store §2 forbids.
Rate as anything but a floor. A pacer that caught up after a slow broker by publishing a burst would replay at a rate nobody asked for; the docstring and the runbook state the choice.
Counting messages on the topic that belong to another capture. `IngestCounts` refuses the set instead, loudly and by name. Splitting the count would be machinery for a producer that does not exist.
lessons: task 11: A materialized view created over `helena_normalized_events` in RisingWave 3.0.3 BACKFILLS from the table's existing rows — measured: 10 rows in the table, `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... GROUP BY ...` returned all 10 immediately, and a capture replayed afterwards appeared in it incrementally. So `concept/06-technology.md`'s 'a view added later starts empty rather than backfilling' is about a view over a stream and does NOT describe views over the stored events. What needs replaying is records that never reached the store, not views created late. Do not repeat the note's sentence in a doc without this qualification.

task 11: `IngestCounts` could not tell 'records were lost' from 'a record was consumed twice', because storing an event again is an upsert and `normalized` does not grow — both make normalized + quarantined < consumed. Replay is what makes the second reachable (publish twice, drain once). The `consumed > records` check now runs BEFORE the accounting check so the diagnosis names the right failure; the two error texts are asserted separately in tests/test_normalizer.py.

task 11: A pacing test needs an unpaced control on a second topic or it measures nothing — a slow broker satisfies a 'took at least N seconds' floor on its own. Create both topics before the clock starts, so neither number includes a CreateTopics round trip. 5 records at 2.5/s against the pinned blink: paced 1.6 s, unpaced well under it.

task 11: A script under `scripts/` can be tested for real by running it through `uv run` in a subprocess with an explicit environment — the process environment wins over `.env` in `Settings.load`, so `{**os.environ, **ENVIRONMENT, KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: <fixture>, HELENA_INGEST_TOPIC: <fresh>}` keeps the run off the developer's real topic. What a wrapper gets wrong is argument handling and exit status, and calling `main()` in-process tests neither.

task 11: `helena.normalizer` now imports `helena.broker`. That is allowed and does not weaken the broker boundary — tests/test_broker.py asserts who imports `confluent_kafka`, not who imports `helena.broker` — and the direction (normalizer -> broker) keeps the broker module ignorant of the ingest message shape, which is what makes it swappable.

task 11: The engine is left exactly as it was found after a hand-run: `DELETE FROM helena_normalized_events; DELETE FROM helena_ingest_quarantine; FLUSH` and re-check the counts. A probe materialized view is dropped the same way. The persistent store under scripts/dev-up survives sessions, so a leftover row becomes the next session's mystery.
failed_approaches: task 11: Adding `HELENA_CAPTURE_DIRECTORY` to `helena.config` was considered and rejected before it was written. `Settings.load` resolves all or nothing, so a required variable that only the replay command reads would fail startup for every deployment that never replays — and every test that builds an environment dict would need it (the cost task 10 paid for HELENA_INGEST_TOPIC). A required CLI argument with no default keeps the same fail-loud property.

task 11: Counting the messages on the topic that came from some other capture, so the reconciliation could subtract them, was designed and dropped. There is no second producer in this prototype, the refusal is already loud and names the cause, and the subtraction would have made `consumed` mean something different in the replay path from what it means in `ingest_counts` — two denominators with one name.

task 11: Putting the replay driver in `helena.orchestration` (the README's module map gives orchestration 'replay') was rejected: `concept/03-architecture.md` gives Orchestration replay *from stored results*, an assessment-level concern. Replaying a capture is the producer side of the ingest topic and belongs beside `IngestMessage.headers()`, which is already in `helena.normalizer` for the same reason — the two ends of the wire format are one piece of code.
next_session_should_know: Replay is `uv run scripts/replay_capture.py --captures <dir> <sha256> [--rate N] [--ingest] [--idle-timeout S]`, and `tests/fixtures/captures/` is a capture directory (files are named by their own digest; `data/ingest/` is NOT one — flow-sample.jsonl fails the name check, which is deliberate). Underneath it are two new functions in `helena.normalizer`: `publish_capture(capture, producer, topic, rate=None)` creates the topic, publishes every record with the reference in its headers, flushes, and returns the count; `consume_ingest_topic(consumer, topic, idle_timeout=...)` is a generator turning wire messages into `IngestMessage`s and is the one place that decode happens. A live consumer daemon should call exactly those two, not reimplement the framing. Five things worth knowing before touching this. (1) A view added over `helena_normalized_events` BACKFILLS — measured, and it contradicts `concept/06-technology.md`; docs/runbook.md §5 and the new §8 carry the measurement, and the concept note itself has not been edited (concept/ outranks code, so that correction is the operator's). Task 12's flatten views therefore do not need to exist before data flows; what needs to exist before data flows is the events table. (2) `IngestCounts._reconciles` changed order: `consumed > records` is now checked first and says 'consumed more than once', because the upsert makes a double-consumed run arithmetically identical to a lossy one. No field changed and no caller changed. (3) `--ingest` makes the replay process the consumer too. That is right only while nothing else consumes the topic — which is the case today. (4) `--rate` is a floor, not a schedule, and a rate of zero or less is refused rather than read as 'unpaced'. (5) The runbook grew §8 (replay, the capture-directory rule, the two-replays-vs-two-publishes distinction, and the backfill procedure) and the old §8 troubleshooting table is now §9 with four new rows; README gained a 'Replay' subsection under ingest. Nothing else in the tree moved.
